reranked_evidence.title: Jerusalem completes safety preparation for Tisha B'Av prayers, events - The Jerusalem Post
reranked_evidence.snippet: # Police, Border Guard complete public safety preparations ahead of Tisha B’av. ## Police and Border Guard will deploy both overt and covert forces, as well as special units, in Jerusalem's Old City to ensure law enforcement can swiftly respond to any unusual incidents. Israel Police deployed at 2025 Tisha B’Av prayers and events in Jerusalem. In preparation for the holiday of Tisha B’Av, hundreds of police officers, Border Guard soldiers, and volunteers will be deployed throughout Jerusalem on Wednesday to maintain public safety and direct traffic. Police and Border Guard will deploy both overt and covert forces, as well as special units, to ensure that law enforcement will be able to swiftly respond to any unusual incidents. In preparation for the end of the Tisha B’Av fast, Sultan Suleiman Street, Jericho Road, Ophel Road, and Ma’ale Hashalom Street will be intermittently closed between 4:00 p.m. and 2:00 a.m. Public transportation to the Western Wall will operate on its normal schedule throughout Wednesday and Thursday.

reranked_evidence.snippet: ## A senior security official said that as more US forces arrive in the region, coordination with the militaries will tighten, while the US military is also redeploying F-35 and F-15 aircraft and dozens. As the hours pass and more American forces arrive in the Middle East, coordination between the IDF and US military will naturally tighten, “with the goal of shortening the time it takes to move from routine to emergency readiness,” a senior security official said on Sunday. Another senior security official, who is familiar with the details of the talks with the US Department of Defense, said that at this stage, dozens of American refueling aircraft will be deployed across IDF bases and the Ramon Airport in southern Israel. As part of the buildup of American forces in the Middle East and Israel, the US military is redeploying F-35 aircraft from Britain and F-15 aircraft from Germany, including aircraft specialized in suppressing enemy air defenses and radars.

reranked_evidence.title: Israeli defense-tech firm ASIO raises $15 million for global expansion - Ynetnews
reranked_evidence.snippet: ## Protego Ventures and Aliya Capital Partners led the company’s first funding round; ASIO says its navigation, situational-awareness and command systems are deployed across the IDF and used by defense customers worldwide. Israeli defense-technology company ASIO has raised $15 million in its first funding round as it seeks to expand production, accelerate product development and increase sales to defense customers worldwide. The round was led by Israeli defense-focused venture capital fund Protego Ventures, with Miami-based Aliya Capital Partners serving as co-lead investor. Founded by Tomer and Yaniv Malchi, ASIO develops tactical systems designed for military forces operating in complex environments where communications and satellite navigation may be disrupted. ASIO said its systems are deployed across all branches of the Israel Defense Forces and are also used by defense customers internationally. “This investment deepens our commitment to Israel’s defense-tech ecosystem, and we’re proud to co-lead alongside Protego Ventures in backing Tomer, Yaniv, and the ASIO team as they scale their platform to defense customers around the world,” Kestin said.

reranked_evidence.snippet: ## The U.S. military said Sunday it had ended its latest round of airstrikes on Iran, which included targeting Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard over an attack that killed American troops in Jordan. DUBAI, United Arab Emirates (AP) — The United States launched more airstrikes at Iran on Sunday in response to the killing of U.S. troops, and Iran fired missiles toward Jordan that risked widening the conflict into neighboring Israel. The U.S. military said the latest strikes targeted Iran’s paramilitary Revolutionary Guard to retaliate for Friday’s killing of troops in Jordan. The U.S. military’s Central Command said it hit “Iranian military coastal surveillance and air defense facilities, maritime capabilities and missile and drone storage sites.” It said the attack was designed to degrade Iran’s ability to control the strait and “swiftly punish Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces,” a power base in Iran’s theocracy that controls its ballistic missile arsenal.

reranked_evidence.title: For Taylor Swift, Madison Square Garden’s Controversial Cameras Briefly Went Dark - WIRED
reranked_evidence.snippet: Madison Square Garden owner James Dolan has insisted that the face-recognition system and array of surveillance cameras deployed at his venues is “very, very useful for security”—a big reason why MSG “is the most secure venue in the country.”. On the night of July 2, security in and around the Garden was particularly intense. July 2 was, of course, the kickoff to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding celebration, an approximately 100-person rehearsal dinner at Madison Square Garden’s Infosys Theater. And yet, on that extremely sensitive evening, Dolan’s MSG locked nearly all of its security team out of the network of surveillance cameras inside the arena, according to an internal document reviewed by WIRED. According to the internal document, an MSG executive ordered on July 2 a seven-hour lockdown of the Garden’s video management system, made by the security tech company Genetec, “due to a client privacy request.” Security staffers who ordinarily monitor the building’s internal cameras and the accompanying face-recognition software were barred from doing so.
